details: Damerau (December 25, 1931 – January 27, 2009) was a pioneer of research on natural language processing and data mining. After earning his B.A. from Cornell University in 1953, he spent most of his career at IBM, in the Thomas J. Watson Research Center. He holds a PhD from Yale University. One of his most influential and ground-breaking papers was "A technique for computer detection and correction of spelling errors" published in 1964. He also developed and patented for IBM the first algorithm for placing hyphens automatically in words. In 1971 he published the book "Markov Models and Linguistic Theory : An Experimental Study of a Model for English." After being active in research for over four decades, Fred Damerau died on January 27, 2009.

explainer.lead: Frederick J. Damerau was an early researcher in natural language processing and data mining. His work helped computers handle written language, including detecting and correcting spelling errors and placing hyphens automatically.

tiers.eli5: Frederick Damerau helped teach computers to work with words, a bit like giving a very literal proofreader a set of instructions. He studied how a computer could spot spelling mistakes and suggest corrections. He also worked on automatically deciding where words could be split with a hyphen.
tiers.practitioner: Damerau's work is relevant as early research in computational language processing, spelling correction, automatic hyphenation, and data mining. His 1964 spelling-error paper and 1971 book on Markov models and English are useful starting points for studying that history. They are research works, not descriptions of a ready-to-install modern tool.
tiers.paperLevel: Frederick J. Damerau (1931–2009) conducted research in natural language processing and data mining. His originating work on computerized spelling correction is the 1964 paper "A technique for computer detection and correction of spelling errors." His 1971 book, "Markov Models and Linguistic Theory: An Experimental Study of a Model for English," presents an experimental study of a Markov model for English.

explainer.example: When a document contains a misspelled word, the problem addressed by Damerau's 1964 paper is to have a computer detect that error and correct it rather than relying entirely on a human proofreader.
